an5.148:3.2: _Dāra_ (“spouse”) is sometimes grammatically masculine, in which case _dārā_ here is the plural “spouses”, and sometimes feminine, in which case it may also be plural or the singular “spouse”. When the compound _puttadāra_ is resolved, it is typically the plural “spouses”, so I understand this as the default meaning ([sn3.10:4.4](), [an10.74:2.2]()). Indian society accepted a variety of marital arrangements as valid forms of marriage, including polygamy and the Gandharva marriage, a love-match that is not formalized yet still recognized.
